species.real: The Old Course at St Andrews is public land, and it closes for golf on Sundays so townsfolk can walk, picnic and exercise their dogs on it.
species.name: Divotling

dex.text: Lives on the links, where the sea wind lifts the turf. Golfers are asked to replace their divots. This one would rather not be replaced, thank you.
dex.fact: Golf has been played on the links at St Andrews since at least the early 1400s, and the Old Course is often called the home of golf.

species.real: Golf is so old in Scotland that James II banned it in 1457 because it was keeping men from their archery practice.
species.name: Hellbunker

dex.text: Lies in wait in the middle of the fairway with a mouthful of sand and a face like a wall. Plenty have gone in. Fewer have come out in one shot, and none of them were smiling.
dex.fact: Hell Bunker, on the 14th hole of the Old Course, is one of the most famous hazards in golf. Its steep face is built from stacked layers of turf, which greenkeepers call revetting.
